source_text: Ἀποδεξάμενοι δὲ τούτων τὴν ἑρμηνείαν τῶν λέ ξεων, καὶ τὴν ἀπολογίαν, ἀνεκρίναμεν τοὺς αἰτιαθέντας παρὰ τούτων, ὡς λέγοντας μίαν ὑπόστασιν, μὴ ἆρα ὡς Σαβέλλιος φρονεῖ, οὕτω καὶ οὗτοι λέγου σιν ἐπὶ ἀναιρέσει τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος, ἢ ὡς ἀνουσίου ὄντος τοῦ Υἱοῦ, ἢ ἀνυποστάτου τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος; Οἱ δὲ καὶ αὐτοὶ διεβεβαιώσαντο μήτε τοῦτο λέγειν, μήτε οὕτω πεφρονηκέναι πώποτε· ἀλλ' ὑπόστασιν μὲν λέγομεν, ἡγούμενοι ταὐτὸν εἶναι εἰπεῖν ὑπόστασιν καὶ οὐσίαν· μίαν δὲ φρονοῦμεν, διὰ τὸ ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Πατρὸς εἶναι τὸν Υἱὸν, καὶ διὰ τὴν ταυτότητα τῆς φύσεως· μίαν γὰρ θεότητα, καὶ μίαν εἶναι τὴν ταύτης φύσιν πιστεύομεν, καὶ οὐκ ἄλλην μὲν τὴν τοῦ Πατρὸς, ξένην δὲ τούτου τὴν τοῦ Υἱοῦ, καὶ τὴν τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος. Ἀμέλει κἀκεῖ οἱ αἰτιαθέντες ὡς εἰρηκότες τρεῖς ὑποστάσεις συνετίθεντο τούτοις· καὶ αὐτοὶ δὲ οἱ εἰρηκότες μίαν οὐσίαν τὰ ἐκείνων ὥσπερ ἡρμήνευσαν καὶ ὡμολόγουν, καὶ ἀνεθεματίζετο παρ' ἀμφοτέρων τῶν μερῶν Ἄρειός τε ὡς Χριστομάχος, καὶ Σαβέλλιος καὶ Παῦλος ὁ Σαμοσατεὺς ὡς ἀσεβεῖς, καὶ Οὐαλεντῖνος καὶ Βασιλείδης ὡς ἀλλότριοι τῆς ἀληθείας, Μανιχαῖος δὲ ὡς ἐφευρετὴς κακῶν· πάντες τε τῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ χάριτι, καὶ μετὰ τὰς τοιαύτας ἑρμηνείας ὁμοῦ συντίθενται τῶν τοιούτων λέξεων βελτίονα καὶ ἀκριβεστέραν εἶναι τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ παρὰ τῶν Πατέρων ὁμολογηθεῖσαν πί στιν, καὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ τοῖς ταύτης ἀρκεῖσθαι μᾶλλον καὶ χρᾶσθαι ῥήμασιν. Ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ περὶ τῆς κατὰ σάρκα οἰκονομίας τοῦ Σωτῆρος, ἐπειδὴ καὶ περὶ τούτου ἐδόκουν φιλονεικεῖν τινες πρὸς ἀλλήλους, ἀνεκρίναμεν καὶ τούτους κἀκείνους, καὶ ἅπερ ὡμολόγουν οὗτοι, συνετίθεντο κἀκεῖνοι, ὅτι οὐχ ὡς εἰς τοὺς προφήτας «ἐγέ νετο ὁ Λόγος Κυρίου,» οὕτω καὶ εἰς ἅγιον ἄνθρωπον ἐνεδήμησεν ἐπὶ συντελείᾳ τῶν αἰώνων, ἀλλ' αὐτὸς ὁ Λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο· καὶ ἐν μορφῇ Θεοῦ ὑπάρχων, ἔλαβε δούλου μορφὴν, ἔκ τε τῆς Μαρίας τὸ κατὰ σάρκα γεγένηται ἄνθρωπος δι' ἡμᾶς, καὶ οὕτω τελείως καὶ ὁλοκλήρως τὸ ἀνθρώπινον γένος ἐλευθερούμενον ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐν αὐτῷ, καὶ ζωο ποιούμενον ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν, εἰσάγεται εἰς τὴν βασι λείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν. Ὡμολόγουν γὰρ καὶ τοῦτο, ὅτι οὐ σῶμα ἄψυχον, οὐδ' ἀναίσθητον, οὐδ' ἀνόητον εἶχεν ὁ Σωτήρ. Οὐδὲ γὰρ οἷόν τε ἦν, τοῦ Κυρίου δι' ἡμᾶς ἀνθρώπου γενομένου, ἀνόητον εἶναι τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ, οὐδὲ σώματος μόνου, ἀλλὰ καὶ ψυχῆς ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ Λόγῳ σωτηρία γέγονεν· Υἱός τε ὢν ἀληθῶς τοῦ Θεοῦ, γέγονε καὶ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου· καὶ μονογενὴς ὢν Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ, γέγονεν ὁ αὐτὸς καὶ πρωτότοκος ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς. Διὸ οὔθ' ἕτερος μὲν ἦν ὁ πρὸ τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἕτερος δὲ ὁ μετὰ Ἀβραάμ· οὐδ' ἕτερος μὲν ἦν ὁ τὸν Λάζαρον ἐγείρας, ἕτερος δὲ ὁ πυνθανόμενος περὶ αὐτοῦ· ἀλλ' ὁ αὐτὸς ἦν ἀνθρωπίνως μὲν λέγων, «Ποῦ Λάζαρος κεῖται;» θεϊκῶς δὲ τοῦτον ἀνεγείρων· ὁ αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν σωματικῶς μὲν ὡς ἄνθρωπος πτύων, θεϊκῶς δὲ ὡς Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀνοίγων τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ ἐκ γενετῆς τυφλοῦ· καὶ σαρκὶ μὲν πάσχων, ὡς εἶπεν ὁ Πέτρος, θεϊκῶς δὲ ἀνοίγων τὰ μνήματα, καὶ ἀνεγείρων τοὺς νεκρούς.
thought_title: The two parties agree on one being and on the incarnation
orientation: Athanasius and the bishops with him continue reporting the examination of the two Antiochene groups, now turning to those accused of saying one person and then to the incarnation.
pass_a_gloss: And having accepted the interpretation of these words and the defense, we examined those accused by them, as saying one person, whether perhaps as Sabellius thinks, so also these speak for the removal of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, or as the Son being without being, or the Holy Spirit without person? But they themselves also affirmed that they neither say this, nor have ever thought so; but we say person, thinking that it is the same to say person and being; and we think one, because the Son is from the being of the Father, and because of the sameness of the nature; for we believe that there is one divinity, and one nature of this, and not one nature of the Father, and foreign from this the nature of the Son, and the nature of the Holy Spirit. Indeed there also those accused as having said three persons agreed with these; and those who had said one being interpreted the things of those as it were and confessed, and Arius was condemned by both parties as fighter against Christ, and Sabellius and Paul of Samosata as impious, and Valentinus and Basilides as strangers to the truth, and Manichaeus as inventor of evils; and all by the grace of God, and after such interpretations, agree together that the faith confessed in Nicaea by the Fathers is better and more exact than such words, and for the future to be content rather with the words of this and to use them. But also the matter concerning the plan of salvation according to the flesh of the Savior, since also about this some seemed to quarrel with one another, we examined both these and those, and what these confessed, those also agreed, that not as to the prophets the Word of the Lord came, so also into a holy man he dwelt at the end of the ages, but the Word himself became flesh; and being in the form of God, he took the form of a slave, and from Mary according to the flesh he became man for us, and thus perfectly and completely the human race being freed from sin in him, and being made alive from the dead, is brought into the kingdom of the heavens. For they confessed also this, that the Savior did not have a body without soul, nor without sensation, nor without understanding. For it was not possible, since the Lord became man for us, that his body be without understanding, nor has salvation come about of the body only, but also of the soul in the Word himself; and being truly Son of God, he became also son of man; and being only-begotten Son of God, the same became also firstborn among many brothers. Therefore neither was one the Son of God before Abraham, and another the one after Abraham; nor was one the one who raised Lazarus, and another the one who asked about him; but the same was speaking humanly, Where does Lazarus lie? and raising him divinely; and the same was spitting bodily as man, and divinely as Son of God opening the eyes of the one blind from birth; and suffering in the flesh, as Peter said, and divinely opening the tombs, and raising the dead.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'person' for this disputed term, and the passage is precisely about how the one-person group uses it as equivalent to being.
The glossary requires 'being' for οὐσία, and the passage contrasts person and being as the two terminologies.
The glossary requires 'condemn' for ἀναθεματίζειν, and the passive here fits the collective condemnation by both parties.
The glossary requires 'plan of salvation' for οἰκονομία, and the phrase 'according to the flesh' specifies the incarnation.
ἀνόητος means lacking intellect or understanding, not lacking a soul; the passage contrasts it with ψυχή (soul) later.
The glossary requires 'flesh' for σάρξ, and this echoes John 1:14 exactly.

pass_b_english: After accepting their explanation of these words and their defense, we examined those whom they had accused of saying one person, to see whether they were thinking as Sabellius does and saying this to do away with the Son and the Holy Spirit, or as though the Son were without being or the Holy Spirit without person. They too affirmed that they had never said this or thought this way. “We say person,” they said, “because we think that saying person and saying being are the same thing. We think one because the Son is from the being of the Father and because of the sameness of nature. For we believe that there is one divinity and one nature of that divinity, and not one nature of the Father and a different, foreign nature of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.” Indeed, those who had been accused of saying three persons also agreed with them, and those who had said one being interpreted and accepted what the others said. Both sides condemned Arius as an enemy of Christ, and Sabellius and Paul of Samosata as impious, and Valentinus and Basilides as strangers to the truth, and Mani as an inventor of evils. By the grace of God, after these explanations, they all agree together that the faith confessed by the Fathers at Nicaea is better and more precise than such words, and that from now on they are content with and use its language.

But since some also seemed to be quarreling with one another about the plan of salvation of the Savior according to the flesh, we examined both groups about this as well, and what the one group confessed, the other also agreed to: that the Word of the Lord did not come to dwell in a holy man at the end of the ages as he came to the prophets, but the Word himself became flesh (John 1:14). And being in the form of God, he took the form of a servant (Philippians 2:6-7), and from Mary he became human according to the flesh for us. In this way the human race is completely and wholly freed from sin in him, made alive from the dead, and brought into the kingdom of heaven. For they also confessed this: that the Savior did not have a body without a soul, without sensation, or without understanding. For it was not possible, when the Lord became human for us, that his body should be without understanding, nor was salvation only of the body, but also of the soul, in the Word himself. Being truly Son of God, he also became son of man; and being the only Son of God, the same one also became firstborn among many brothers. Therefore there was not one Son of God before Abraham and another after Abraham; nor was there one who raised Lazarus and another who asked about him. The same one spoke in human fashion when he said, “Where does Lazarus lie?” (John 11:34), and raised him in divine fashion. The same one spat bodily as a man, and in divine fashion as Son of God opened the eyes of the man blind from birth (John 9:1). And he suffered in the flesh, as Peter said (1 Peter 4:1), and in divine fashion opened the tombs and raised the dead.

problems.quote: to do away with the Son and the Holy Spirit, or as though the Son had no being or the Holy Spirit had no person
problems.source_quote: ἐπὶ ἀναιρέσει τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος, ἢ ὡς ἀνουσίου ὄντος τοῦ Υἱοῦ, ἢ ἀνυποστάτου τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος
problems.why: Source asks whether they say one person to abolish Son and Spirit, or as if Son is without being or Spirit without person. English merges two distinct questions.
problems.fix: to do away with the Son and the Holy Spirit, or as though the Son were without being or the Holy Spirit without person
problems.ruling: Source has two distinct alternatives (ἢ...ἢ), but English merges into one question with 'or as though'.

edits.old: to do away with the Son and the Holy Spirit, or as though the Son had no being or the Holy Spirit had no person
edits.new: to do away with the Son and the Holy Spirit, or as though the Son were without being or the Holy Spirit without person

fixed: The English 'had no being' and 'had no person' slightly misstate the source's 'ἀνουσίου ὄντος' and 'ἀνυποστάτου', which mean 'being without being' and 'without person'. Changed to 'were without being' and 'without person' to match the source more closely.

last_rejected.why: Χριστομάχος means 'one who fights against Christ', not merely 'enemy.' The English loses the active combative sense.
last_rejected.fix: as one who fights against Christ
last_rejected.ruling: 'Enemy of Christ' is within normal range for Χριστομάχος; 'combative' nuance is implied, not lost.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἀνοίγων τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ ἐκ γενετῆς τυφλοῦ
last_rejected.why: The healing of the man born blind is John 9:6-7, not John 9:1.
last_rejected.ruling: John 9:1 introduces the man born blind; the whole healing narrative is reasonably cited as 9:1.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἐν μορφῇ Θεοῦ ὑπάρχων, ἔλαβε δούλου μορφὴν
last_rejected.why: The citation should be Philippians 2:7, not 2:6-7. The quoted words 'being in the form of God, he took the form of a servant' are from verse 7 specifically; verse 6 adds different content not quoted.
last_rejected.ruling: The source combines content spanning Phil 2:6-7; citing both verses is standard and not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: and brought into the kingdom of heaven
last_rejected.source_quote: εἰσάγεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν
last_rejected.why: The English omits that the human race is 'made alive from the dead' (ζωοποιούμενον ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν) before being brought into the kingdom.
last_rejected.fix: made alive from the dead, and brought into the kingdom of heaven
last_rejected.ruling: English includes 'made alive from the dead' just before 'brought into the kingdom'; no omission.

last_rejected.quote: and those who had said one being interpreted and accepted what the others said
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ αὐτοὶ δὲ οἱ εἰρηκότες μίαν οὐσίαν τὰ ἐκείνων ὥσπερ ἡρμήνευσαν καὶ ὡμολόγουν
last_rejected.why: The English says 'interpreted and accepted' but the Greek says 'interpreted and confessed/agreed to' (ἡρμήνευσαν καὶ ὡμολόγουν). 'Accepted' is weaker than 'confessed' and loses the reciprocal confessional nature.
last_rejected.ruling: ὡμολόγουν here means 'agreed/consented'; 'accepted' is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: The Greek is passive: 'was condemned by both sides,' not active 'Both sides condemned.' The agency is slightly shifted though the overall sense is similar. However, the passive emphasizes that Arius etc. were condemned by both parties together, which is significant for the unity theme.
last_rejected.ruling: Passive-to-active voice shift preserves meaning; 'both sides condemned' is accurate and clear.

last_rejected.quote: they are content with and use its language
last_rejected.source_quote: τοῖς ταύτης ἀρκεῖσθαι μᾶλλον καὶ χρᾶσθαι ῥήμασιν
last_rejected.why: The English 'its language' translates 'ῥήμασιν' (words), but misses 'μᾶλλον' (rather/more), which emphasizes preferring Nicaea's words over the disputed terms. The 'rather' is significant for the comparative force.
last_rejected.fix: they are rather content with and use its words
last_rejected.ruling: 'μᾶλλον' is subsumed in 'are content with and use'; comparative nuance is minor, not misleading.
